title: Month shifts gave no clear local solar weekday pattern in global M5.5+ earthquakes in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested all seven local mean solar weekdays in 12,848 global ComCat earthquakes with preferred magnitude at least 5.5 in 2000-2025. A prior UTC weekend test left five count-contrast directions untested. We used a rank-six quadratic statistic and exact count means and covariances from circular integer-day shifts within UTC months. In 19,999 simulations, the primary p value was 0.91785. The largest observed departure from the shift mean was a 3.756% Monday deficit. An approximate simultaneous 95% year-resampling band had a radius of 10.781 percentage points. UTC, magnitude, depth, era and whole-year shift checks gave p values above 0.4. The full local solar test found no clear pattern missed by the earlier weekend contrast. This is an extension on the same data, not independent confirmation. It does not show equal physical rates or identify a cause. Month boundaries split event groups, local solar dates differ from civil dates, and only 26 years limit inference. Independent date arithmetic found and resolved a timestamp-unit error before publication. The corrected evidence passed a full count audit and an exact repeat. Code, aggregate counts, simulation draws, source hashes and a figure are supplied. External event records stay outside the bundle.

display.caption: Local solar weekday count departures from exact month-shift means. Bars show pointwise year-resampling limits and an approximate simultaneous band. All include zero departure.
